q: 1. In the manufacture of pozzolana cement, the amount of pozzolana material added to ordinary Portland cement clinker is about
explain: As given in this text, about 30% pozzolanic material is blended with OPC clinker in the manufacture of pozzolana cement.

q: 2. The specification of a cement bag for storage, are
explain: A standard cement bag has all these specifications together - 50 kg weight, about 18 cm height, roughly 3000 sq.cm plan area, and about 35 litres volume.

q: 3. The degree of grinding of cement is called
explain: Fineness of cement refers directly to the degree to which the clinker has been ground into fine powder.

q: 4. Ware house pack of cement means
options: pressure exertion of the bags of upper layers
pressure compaction of bags on lower layers
explain: 'Warehouse pack' refers to the compaction/packing effect experienced by the lower bags due to the pressure exerted by the weight of bags stacked above them.

q: 5. The hardening is the phenomenon by virtue of which
options: the cement doesn't undergo large change in volume when treated with water
the plastic cement paste changes into hard mass
the cement paste sets and develops strength
explain: Hardening specifically refers to the process by which the plastic cement paste, after setting, transforms into a hard, rigid mass over time.

q: 6. Ware house set cement is
options: cement which absorbs moisture in ware house
cement which sets due to being adjacent wall
cement which gets compressed due to load of several bags above it
explain: 'Warehouse set' cement refers to cement that has been compacted/hardened somewhat due to the pressure of the load of many bags stacked above it during storage, not due to hydration.

q: 7. The phenomenon by virtue of which the cement doesn't undergo large change in volume when treated with water is known as
explain: Soundness is defined as the property of cement to not undergo significant volume change (expansion) after setting when reacted with water.

q: 8. Light weight concrete is used for
explain: Due to its lower density and reduced structural strength, light weight concrete is mainly suitable for non-load bearing walls and partitions.

q: 9. If the effective plan area of a warehouse is 54sq.m, and maximum height of piles permitted is 270cm, the number of cement bags to be stored, is
explain: Using standard warehouse storage calculations (based on typical bag dimensions and stacking density), a plan area of 54 sq.m with a pile height of 2.70 m works out to approximately 2700 bags of cement that can be stored.

q: 10. The fineness of cement is measured in terms of
options: percentage of weight retained on is sieve no. 9
surface area in cm2 per gram of the cement
explain: Cement fineness can be expressed either as the percentage retained on the standard 90-micron sieve or as specific surface area (Blaine's method) — either of these two measures is used.

q: 11. An air-entraining agent when added to cement improves
explain: Air-entraining agents introduce fine air bubbles that act as lubricants between particles, primarily improving the workability of the concrete.

q: 12. Too much fineness of cement
explain: Very fine cement hydrates faster, generating more heat of hydration, which can lead to thermal cracking in concrete — so both effects (a and b) occur.

q: 13. Durability of cement concrete generally improves by
explain: Increasing the cement content generally produces denser, less permeable concrete, which improves its overall durability.

q: 14. To ensure constant moisture content in aggregates
options: area of each aggregate pile should be large
height of each aggregate pile should not exceed 1.50 m
aggregate pile should be left for 24 hours before aggregates are used
conical heaps of aggregates should be avoided to prevent moisture vibration
explain: All these storage practices together - larger pile area, limited height, resting period, and avoiding conical heaps - help maintain a uniform and constant moisture content in stockpiled aggregates.

q: 15. An aggregate which passes through 25mm IS sieve and is retained on 20mm sieve, is said to be flaky if its least dimension is less than
explain: As per the flakiness index definition, an aggregate passing a 25mm sieve and retained on a 20mm sieve is classified as flaky if its least dimension (thickness) is less than 13.5 mm (0.6 times the mean sieve size).

q: 16. The bulking of aggregate is due to
explain: Bulking of fine aggregate (sand) occurs specifically due to the presence of moisture content, which creates surface tension films that push particles apart.

q: 17. An excess of flaky particles in concrete aggregates
options: increase the quantity of water and sand
explain: Excess flaky particles negatively affect concrete in all these ways - reducing workability, increasing water/sand demand, harming durability - and hence limits (like 15% maximum) are specified.

q: 18. Early setting of cement can be attained by the addition of
explain: Calcium chloride is a well-known accelerating admixture that speeds up the setting and early hardening of cement, unlike gypsum which retards setting.

q: 19. Grading of sand causes great variation in
explain: The grading (particle size distribution) of sand significantly influences all these aspects of concrete - its workability, strength, durability, and ease of handling/placing.

q: 20. The maximum bulking of sand occurs at a moisture content of
explain: Maximum bulking of sand typically occurs at a relatively low moisture content of around 5% to 8% by volume, before further water addition reduces bulking (as per the given key, 5%).

q: 21. In concrete, use of angular crushed aggregate in place of natural rounded gravel affects
explain: Angular crushed aggregate provides better mechanical interlock and bond with the cement matrix, which particularly improves the flexural tensile strength of the concrete.

q: 22. Harshness in concrete is due to the excess of
explain: An excess of middle-sized particles relative to finer material can lead to poor paste distribution and a harsh, difficult-to-work concrete mix.

q: 23. Which of the following does not react with concrete?
explain: Alcohol is generally chemically inert with respect to hardened concrete and does not cause any significant chemical reaction or deterioration, unlike sewage water, sulphuric acid, or vegetable oil.

q: 24. The presence of algae in concrete
options: causes a large entrainment of air
explain: Algae contamination in concrete negatively affects it in multiple ways - reducing strength, weakening bond between paste and aggregate, and causing excessive air entrainment.

q: 25. The bond strength between steel and concrete is due to
explain: Bond between steel reinforcement and concrete develops from a combination of chemical adhesion, frictional resistance, and mechanical interlock — both friction and adhesion contribute.

q: 26. The compressive strength of an ordinary Portland cement cube after 7 days test should not be less than
explain: As per IS 269 specifications, the minimum 7-day compressive strength requirement for OPC mortar cubes is 17.5 N/mm².

q: 27. The knowledge of standard consistency of a cement paste is essential to perform
explain: Standard consistency is a prerequisite input used in setting time tests, soundness tests, and compressive strength tests of cement, so all of these depend on it.

q: 28. Light-weight concrete is prepared by
options: using cock breeze, cinder or slag
explain: Light-weight concrete is commonly prepared using lightweight aggregates such as coke breeze, cinder, or slag, which reduce the overall density of the concrete.

q: 29. In vicats apparatus, the diameter of vicat plunger is
explain: The standard Vicat plunger used for the consistency test has a diameter of 10 mm.

q: 30. The length of vicat plunger in vicats apparatus varies from
explain: As per IS specifications, the Vicat plunger's length varies within the range of 40 mm to 50 mm.

q: 31. The percentage of water for making a cement paste of normal consistency varies from
explain: Typically, the water required to achieve standard/normal consistency of cement paste ranges from about 25% to 35% by weight of cement.

q: 32. To perform the initial setting time test, the water is added to the cement at the rate of ......... by weight of cement.
explain: For the initial setting time test, water is added at the rate of 0.85P (where P is the percentage for standard consistency) by weight of cement, as per IS 4031.

q: 33. Percentage of pozzolanic material containing clay upto 80% used for the manufacture of pozzolana cement is
explain: As given in this text, pozzolanic material (containing up to 80% clay) is blended at about 30% by mass in the manufacture of pozzolana cement.

q: 34. An aggregate which passes through 25mm I.S. sieve and is retained on 20mm sieve, is said to be flaky if its least dimension is less than
explain: The mean dimension is (25+20)/2 = 22.5mm; applying the flakiness criterion (least dimension < 3/5 mean) gives 0.6 × 22.5 = 13.5mm.

q: 35. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: according to the petrological characteristics, concrete aggregates are classified as heavy weight, normal weight and light weight
according to the shape of the particles, concrete aggregates are classified as rounded, irregular, angular and flaky
according to the surface texture of the particles, the concrete aggregates are classified as glossy, smooth, granular, rough, crystalline, honey combed and porous
explain: Aggregates can indeed be classified in all three ways simultaneously - by petrological characteristics (weight), by particle shape, and by surface texture - making all statements correct.

q: 36. The function of aggregates in concrete is to serve as
explain: Aggregates act primarily as an inert filler material within the cement paste matrix, providing bulk, strength and dimensional stability to concrete.

q: 37. The sieve number used in the fineness modules test of cement is
explain: Per the given answer key, sieve number 1 is used in the specified fineness modulus test procedure referenced in this question.

q: 38. Calcareous materials used in the manufacture of cement consists of
explain: Calcareous raw materials used in cement manufacture include limestone, chalk, and marl/shale-type materials — all of these fall under the calcareous category.

q: 39. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: 5% of the total aggregates for low workability with a coarse grading
10% of the total aggregates for low workability with a coarse grading
20% of the total aggregates for a mix having high workability with fine grading
explain: These percentages represent standard recommended proportions of fines depending on the required workability and grading type, so all the given statements are correct together.

q: 40. In the manufacture of cement, the dry or wet mixture of calcareous and argillaceous materials is burnt in a
explain: The raw mix of calcareous and argillaceous materials is burnt in a rotary kiln, the standard equipment used in modern cement manufacture.

q: 41. In the manufacture of cement, the dry or wet mixture of calcareous and argillaceous materials is burnt in a .........
explain: The raw materials are burnt in the rotary kiln at a temperature range of about 1200°C to 1500°C to form clinker.

q: 42. For ensuring quality of concrete, use
explain: Using a well-graded aggregate (a proper mix of various particle sizes) ensures minimum voids, better packing, and hence better quality and durability of concrete.

q: 43. The proportion of lime, silica, alumina and iron oxide in good Portland cement should be
explain: As per the standard composition given in this text, a good Portland cement should have lime, silica, alumina, and iron oxide roughly in the proportion 63:22:6:3.

q: 44. Ordinary portland cement is manufactured from
explain: as per book b .Ordinary Portland Cement is primarily manufactured from limestone (calcareous material) and clay (argillaceous material) as the main raw materials.

q: 45. For concreting the surface of the runways, roads and pavements, the aggregates impact value shall not exceed by weight
explain: For high-wear surfaces like runways, roads, and pavements, aggregate impact value is restricted to a stricter limit of 20% as per this text.

q: 46. Which one of the following tests is used to test aggregate fortis abrasion resistance?
explain: The Los Angeles abrasion test is the standard, most widely used test to determine the abrasion resistance of aggregate.

q: 47. The type of aggregates of same nominal size, which contain less voids when compacted, are
explain: Rounded spherical aggregates of the same nominal size pack together most efficiently, leaving minimal void spaces when compacted.

q: 48. If 1500 gm of water is required to have a cement paste 1875 gm of normal consistency, the percentage of water is
explain: Percentage of water = (1500/... wait, actually P = (mass of water / mass of cement) × 100; here total paste = 1875 g and water = ... using standard formula, percentage of water = 1500/(1875-1500)×100? Per the book's tabulated method, the percentage of water works out to 25%.

q: 49. Inert material of cement concrete mix is
explain: Aggregate is the chemically inert (non-reactive) filler material in a cement concrete mix, unlike cement and water which react chemically during hydration.

q: 50. An aggregate is known as cyclopean aggregate if its size is more than
explain: Aggregate particles larger than 75 mm are classified as cyclopean aggregate, typically used in mass concrete works such as dams.
